text.title: Ios Signing And Provisioning Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable signing signals to a rule from `content/01-core-rules.xml`. Every leaf names either a concrete rule id or `skip-this-methodology` when the case is out of scope. Max depth = 4.

decision-tree.root-question: Is the app distributed through Apple signing at all (App Store, TestFlight, ad-hoc or enterprise builds)?

conclusion.verdict: skip-this-methodology: no Apple signing chain to document (web app, simulator-only, or Android-only)

branch.question: Does a complete inventory exist: every certificate, profile, API key and APNs key with identifier, expiry and storage location?

conclusion.verdict: build the inventory from the developer portal first; nothing else in this document can be checked without it

branch.question: Does any asset expire within 30 days, or is any private key stored outside the named secret store?

conclusion.verdict: rotate now, move key material into the secret store, add rotation entries with a named person

branch.question: Is push on a yearly APNs certificate, or is any CI key issued with the Admin role?

conclusion.verdict: migrate push to a .p8 token key and reissue CI keys per pipeline with the least role
run the procedure: fill the per-config aps-environment map, revocation runbook and client Team ID, then hand off for review

text.example: Observable: App Store distribution; inventory built (1 distribution cert, 2 profiles, 1 ASC key with Developer role, 1 APNs .p8); nothing expires within 30 days; keys in the CI secret store → run-the-checklist → procedure in content/04-procedure.xml, with the client Team ID recorded per r-client-account-owns-the-app.
